newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Two killed in govt hunt for Tajik rebel group.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in govt hunt for Tajik rebel group.

text.p: A government hunt for a rebel band which seized foreign aid workers in Tajikistan last month has left two dead but much of the group and one of its leaders are still at large, official sources said on Sunday.
Officials in the former Soviet republic said one of the rebels had been killed in fighting on Saturday along with a fighter on the government's side.
"An intensive search for the armed group is continuing in the Obigarm region," one official told Reuters in Dushanbe, the capital of the Central Asian state.

The government said one of the group's leaders, Bakhrom Sadirov, had been captured on Friday along with 19 of his fighters in a two-pronged attack by government forces and those of the Islamist opposition on his base near Obigarm, 80 km (50 miles) east of Dushanbe.
But on Sunday, the sources said 40 members of the group, inlcuding its main leader, Bakhrom's brother Rizvon Sadirov, were still at large.
Sadirov's men took Russian and Western hostages for two weeks last month and won the safe passage of Rizvon and a group of rebels from neighbouring Afghanistan before releasing them.
It was the second hostage-taking by the maverick commander in three months.
The government hunt is politically important as the operation has been carried out with the cooperation of Islamic opposition guerrillas.
The Tajik government and the Islamic opposition have been embroiled in a bitter four-year civil war, but signed a U.N.-sponsored peace accord in December.

A week ago the two sides signed a military agreement in Moscow which builds on the shaky accord with a four-phase plan to integrate armed opposition units into the Tajik army. A ceasefire appears to be holding.
